brief: Tonight is Push B, your second day back after taking Saturday off. That rest day worked — on Sunday you pressed 220 for 10 on the leg press where the same 220 only gave you 8 back on the 18th, and your rest between sets was shorter. So tonight is not a day for brakes, it is a day to spend that freshness in the right places. Start with the Smith overhead press and actually do it — it got skipped entirely last Push B, and the last time you pressed it was July 12, fifteen days ago. Same weights as that day, 95, 105, then 115 twice, but the job is 7 and 8 reps instead of the 6 you did every set. Do it first, while you are fresh, and set up properly on a bench this time. The one real raise tonight is the chest press: you were already under 165 for 8 on Thursday, so 165 is your top set now instead of 157.5, and the ask is to turn that 8 into 10. Three things deliberately do not go up. The cable crossover comes DOWN to 25 per handle — your top set at 27.5 has died early twice, 10 reps two weeks ago and 9 reps last week, against a card asking for 12, and a weight you cannot finish is not a heavier weight, it is a shorter set. Lateral raises run the exact ladder you ran last Monday, 12.5 then 15, 15, 17.5, because your side delts visibly run out inside a session — on Thursday your cable raises fell 10.5 to 9 to 7.5. And the reverse grip pushdowns stay put, because the tail end of your last push day came apart: rope pushdowns went 60.5 for 8, then 57.5 for 7, then 52.5 for 9, stripping weight twice and still never reaching 10. Chase clean reps at the end of the night, not bigger numbers. On the dips, same assistance as last week, and the target is 12 on all three sets — you got 10, 10, 12 last time, so it is one good set and two to catch up. Two notes on the cable stack: your old 24 and 25.5 and 54 were never real loads. The add-on weights read 1.25 per handle, so those were really 23.75, 25 and 53.75 — the numbers on your card tonight are the same effort, just written honestly. Conditioning: easy is fine today, a walk or fifteen minutes on the elliptical after you lift, nothing that costs you tomorrow. Last thing, and it needs you, not me. Your Legs B card on Wednesday is going to show 'hanging leg raise, 2 sets of 60 seconds' — when that slot was swapped off planks it kept the plank's seconds, and you actually do these in reps. I am not allowed to edit your plan on my own, so bring it up in a Claude session before Wednesday along with the overhead press setup and I will fix both properly.

flags.note: Second training day back after Saturday off. The rest day worked — Sunday's leg press was your best yet at 220.
Do the Smith overhead press FIRST tonight. It was skipped entirely last Push B and has not been done since July 12.
Week 2 of a 4-week build block. One raise tonight — the chest press to 165. The cable crossover comes down on purpose.

overrides.reason: This got skipped entirely last Push B, so the last real data is July 12: 95, 105, 115, 115 for exactly 6 reps every set. Six is the bottom of the range, so nothing earned more weight — same four loads, and the job is 7 and 8. Do it first while you are fresh, and use a bench.

On Thursday you pressed 165 for 8 on this machine, but this day still wanted to stop at 157.5 because that is what you did here a week ago. You have already been under 165, so it is your top set tonight and the job is turning that 8 into 10. Every weight on the ladder is one you have lifted.

Same ladder as last Monday, on purpose. Your side delts run out inside a session — on Thursday your cable raises fell from 10.5 to 9 to 7.5, and the week before from 10.5 to 7.5. 17.5 for 12 is already the most you have done here, so you get one set on it, not two.

The top set comes down to 25 per handle. At 27.5 you got 10 reps two weeks ago and 9 last week, against a card asking for 12 — twice now that set has died early. 25 is where your reps actually hold. Own 12 there and 27.5 comes back.

You finished on 90 for 12 last week and were holding 90 for 14 back in January, so a second working set at 90 is ground you already own. The pin does not move past 90 — this machine jumps in 7.5s and you have not put 15 reps on 90 yet.

The stack does not go up tonight. You have been working at what you wrote as 54 — really 53.75 — for 10, 10 and 11 reps, which is inside the range but not the top of it. Same loads, and the ask is 12 on the second set. Two twelves and it moves to 55.

14 and 12 last time is short of the 15 this slot asks for, so both loads stay put and you chase reps. Your last push day fell apart right here — rope pushdowns went 60.5 for 8, 57.5 for 7, 52.5 for 9, stripping weight twice and never reaching 10. Make these two clean.

This day still wanted to give you 22.5 and 24 because that is what you pulled here a week ago, but you have used 27.5 on both Thursday and Friday. Start there. You got a clean 15 on the first set both days and then faded — the whole job is a clean 15 on set two.

dissent.progression: Move the whole ladder up to 150, 157.5, 165 — he was already under 165 for 8 on Thursday and this day would otherwise repeat a weight he has beaten.
dissent.recovery: Hold all three sets at 157.5 — that is the heaviest load he has actually completed the prescribed reps on, and the one time he tried 165 he got 8.
dissent.why: Recovery built its case on the slot asking 10 to 12 reps. It does not — the accepted July 22 change put this slot at 8 to 10, and the dossier handed both seats the old range. Under the range the app will actually show him, his 165 for 8 on Thursday is a completed set at the bottom of the range, not a failure, which is the opposite of what recovery read it as. Recovery also said outright it was not braking here for fatigue: his chest has had four days. With the fatigue argument withdrawn by the seat that owns it, and the rep argument resting on a number that is not on his card, there is nothing left holding 165 back.

dissent.progression: Hold the ladder at 23.75, 25, 27.5 — nothing goes up until the top set survives 12 clean reps.
dissent.recovery: Bring the top set down to 25 and stay off 27.5 — the reps there have twice come in short of what the card asks.
dissent.why: Both seats agree 27.5 is not working. They differ on whether to keep pointing him at it. Twice now — 10 reps on the 12th, 9 on the 20th — that set has ended three reps early against a card asking 12, and progression's own rule is that a weight is not yours until the reps are there. Leaving 27.5 on the card is prescribing a set he has already failed twice and calling it a hold. 25 is a real notch on that stack, it is where his two good sets landed, and it gives him something he can finish.

dissent.progression: Drop the 12.5 opener and give him two sets on the 17.5s — every weight on that line is one he has already lifted.
dissent.recovery: Run the exact July 20 ladder — 12.5, 15, 15, 17.5 — because his side delts fade inside a session.
dissent.why: Progression is right that he has lifted all of these weights, but it is reading them as a list rather than an order. He took 17.5 once, as the last set, after a ramp. Recovery brought the specific evidence: on both cable lateral raise days his weight fell set to set, 10.5 to 9 to 7.5 on Thursday and 10.5 to 7.5 to 7.5 the week before. Removing the ramp and doubling the hardest set is exactly the shape that evidence argues against. This is a small muscle at the front of a long day and there is no cost to earning it properly.

dissent.progression: Keep the working sets at 53.75 and ask for 12 on the second — the stack does not move, only the rep target.
dissent.recovery: Drop all three sets to 52.5, the weight where he actually reaches 12.
dissent.why: Neither seat wants the stack to go up, so this is only about whether the working sets sit one micro plate lower. He has completed that load four times now at 10 and 11 reps — inside the 10 to 12 this slot asks for, not short of it. Prescribing 52.5 would put a smaller number on the card than work he is already finishing successfully, and an under-prescription is a wrong number the same way an over-prescription is. Recovery also said explicitly this was a notch call and not a fatigue call, so the seat that could have stopped it did not try to.
